items.problem: Ported UWP code referencing Windows.UI.Colors (and, generally, Windows.UI.ColorHelper) fails to compile with CS0234 because those framework classes moved to Microsoft.UI in WinApp SDK, but the bootstrap namespace mass-rewrite only handles Windows.UI.Xaml.
items.evidence: session-log.txt:2231-2232 'error CS0234: The type or namespace name \'Colors\' does not exist in the namespace \'Windows.UI\'' at MainPage.xaml.cs(110,63) and (113,63); fixed at session-log.txt:2284-2287.
items.skill_search: grepped winui-uwp-migration for 'Windows.UI.Colors', 'ColorHelper', 'Colors', and the Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 rewrite (-replace 'Windows\.UI\.Xaml').
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 §3 rewrites only 'Windows.UI.Xaml' -> 'Microsoft.UI.Xaml'. The non-Xaml types that also relocated to Microsoft.UI (Colors, ColorHelper) are never rewritten and no residue rule flags them, so they survive into the build as a compile error.
items.proposed_fix: Add a bootstrap rewrite step in Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 mapping 'Windows.UI.Colors' -> 'Microsoft.UI.Colors' and 'Windows.UI.ColorHelper' -> 'Microsoft.UI.ColorHelper' (trailing word boundary so the Windows.UI.Color STRUCT is preserved), add the same as a residueOnly pattern in unsupported-api-inventory.json, and add a caveat row/note in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md that the helper classes move while the Color struct stays.
items.generalizes: Named-color brushes (SolidColorBrush(Colors.X)) and ColorHelper.FromArgb are pervasive across UWP samples; every UWP app that sets colors from code hits this exact CS0234 after migration. The move is mechanical and deterministic, so fixing it in tooling helps every future scenario.
